title: websocket: Enable websocket as heuristic dissector for TCP
description:
Add a new option to use websocket as heuristic dissector for TCP.

This is useful when the connection setup of a HTTP connection which got
upgraded to a websocket was not recorded.

If this option is disabled the resulting behaviour should be the same
as prior. It is disabled by default.

notes.body:
added 31 commits
  • d08f1588...22700560 - 30 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 0a63c2cb - websocket: Enabled websocket as heuristic dissector for TCP
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3538/diffs?diff_id=210638389&start_sha=d08f15884bf83e0b40691cd3288165c79523caf5)
No preference should be needed as `HEURISTIC_DISABLE` can be used to disable it by default.
How does the user enable it?

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3538/diffs?diff_id=233540194&start_sha=0a63c2cbb09a54b7137f8b1bdf88a27d0ffef718#414697477ceb03b3123bcbf5e46ebafa6177f6e4_882_872)
Analyze -> Enabled Protocols -> websocket_tcp
Ok thx. I have changed it to `HEURISTIC_DISABLE` by default.

The probability to hit the three zero bits and one of the opcodes is 14% (`(3/8)*(6/16)=0.140625`). I did not count the a-z A-Z probability which is partially overlapping.

Wouldn't this be too likely to hit on arbitrary binary data?

Would it make the sense to check the length? https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.2

I think websocket protocol is hard to detect with a heuristic. I would not having this heuristic active on default since it may produce many false positive hits. That‘s the reason why I introduced a dedicated preference for enabling this feature. It should be an active descission when enabling it.

I think you are Right. Additionaly Checking the length is worth to take a look on.
Right, but individual heuristics can also be disabled already (by using `HEURISTIC_DISABLE`), you don't need an additional preference for htis.

After giving it a try I am no longer sure if it is a good idea to check for the length. 

A TCP Segment could contain multiple websocket frames. This could be handeled with a loop.

But I am not sure if it is possible that a TCP segment only contains a portion of a websocket frame. In this case a length check would fail.
